On app load the runtime atomically replaces each configured column's INSERT/UPDATE triggers. Failure to read, drop, or create any trigger aborts the transaction, preserves the prior trigger set, and fails app loading.

On a table the MCP connector enrolled for approved writes, the same transaction then recreates the connector's revision triggers so they fire before the encryption triggers. See `api(at:"connector")` (`revision_trigger_order`).

A trigger seals any value that is not authentic ciphertext for the same field using `benmore_encrypt_plaintext(NEW.<col>, '<table>', '<column>')`. This encrypts plaintext literals beginning `enc:v1:` or `enc:v2:` too. Only decryptable ciphertext for the same table and column is left as it is. This also avoids double-encrypting ciphertext written by key rotation or by recursive trigger execution.

`benmore_encrypt_plaintext(value, table, column)` requires non-empty table and column context, returns NULL for NULL, fails without the owning database key, and always seals non-NULL input as AAD-bound `enc:v2:` AES-256-GCM. For example: `UPDATE notes SET secret = benmore_encrypt_plaintext(:secret, 'notes', 'secret') WHERE id = :id`. Existing `benmore_encrypt(value[, table, column])` remains prefix-idempotent for compatibility; do not use it when prefix-looking plaintext must be preserved as plaintext.

Read path: when the auto-CRUD layer returns rows, the runtime walks the configured fields and evaluates unmask_roles for each row using the role's global or tenant scope. Authorized rows return plaintext; other rows return `****` (see mask_format). See unmask_scope for tenant roots, shared tables, projections and owner rules.

OWNER unmask: put `self` (or `owner`) in unmask_roles to decrypt a row FOR ITS OWNER (per-row, matched on the table's user_id == the session user; `owner` here is never a role named owner, see owner_alias). This is mandatory for per-user private data - a journal/notes/health table encrypted WITHOUT `self` shows the owner their own data as `****`, because masking is otherwise admin/role-only. `self` reveals a row only to the person who already owns it (no new exposure). Combine with admin: `unmask_roles: [self, admin]`.

Idempotent: re-INSERT/re-UPDATE preserves only decryptable ciphertext; v2 ciphertext must match the same table and column AAD. Plaintext beginning `enc:v1:` or `enc:v2:` is encrypted as plaintext by the trigger.

Per-app key. AES key resolution: ENCRYPTION_KEY env var → ENCRYPTION_KEY in env.yaml → auto-generated at start. A generated key is persisted to env.yaml (mode 0600, gitignored) when the app has encrypted fields, or when the app first seals a webhook subscription secret or OAuth token (secret_durability); otherwise it lives only in the process.
